content:
Consider a module Foo with

meta initialize hmm : Unit ← do dbg_trace "hello"

and import that file in Bar with import Foo or public import Foo. Then run lake build (note: this behavior is different than in the language server due to differences in IR loading) to receive an error like

% lake build Bar
✖ [3/3] Building Bar
trace: [...]
error: Bar.lean:1:0: (interpreter) unknown declaration '_private.Foo.0.hmm'
info: stderr:
hello
error: Lean exited with code 1
Some required targets logged failures:
- Bar
error: build failed

Doing any of the following fixes it:

  • using an anonymous meta initialize do dbg_trace "hello", which prints hello and does not create the offending opaque hmm in the first place
  • using (public) meta import Foo with any modifiers on initialize, which always prints hello
  • using public meta initialize, which prints hello (I'm thinking due to passing a certain guard during IR generation or export)
  • using initialize or public initialize, which does not get run (does not print hello) since it's now just a runtime initializer
  • creating a private meta def useHmm := hmm in the same module (Foo), which prints hello

After doing a little digging into source (helped along by Claude), I'm still unsure of exactly why it's happening, but it seems like hmm is expected to be in the declMapExt but isn't. (A local meta def apparently brings it along via the closure of its IR, which is why that fixes it.) But I'm not familiar enough with the pipeline to suggest a principled fix.

(For whatever it's worth, Claude suggests a quick fix would be calling setDeclMeta on decls which satisfy isMarkedMeta in the mkDummyExternDecl branch of lowerDecl in Lean.Compiler.IR.ToIR, or a "more robust" fix of broadening isDeclMeta to also return true on all marked-meta decls.)

Should I make an issue?
Does it reproduce on latest nightly? If so, an issue sounds warranted.
I had a similar error with meta initializecausing unknown declaration not long ago, don't understand any of it though.
